perTerm.notes: All four photos prominently feature timber weatherboard buildings (hotels, a homestead, and a wooden-fronted commercial street), so the tag fits every one.
All four clearly show uniformed military personnel; 364002 also includes a civilian woman but the uniformed soldier is a central subject, so the tag still applies.

Photo 1183189 is a heavily faded sepia view of trees over a braided river valley with no identifiable snow — the distant peaks are washed out to blank paper, so a visitor browsing "Snow" would see a bush/valley scene, while the other three clearly show snow-covered slopes and peaks.
All four show prominent cliff faces; the last (354311) is really a steaming volcanic crater, but its steep eroded crater walls still read plainly as cliffs, so it passes as a borderline fit.

All four fit: flowering daisies (53761), berry-bearing ground cover (54572), violets (26782), and a shrub on a rock face (55823) — the last shares the frame with bare rock but the plant is still a clear subject.
520332 shows an elderly woman with a much younger woman on porch steps — reads as a mother/daughter or generational family pair, not spouses; the other three are clear couple/wedding portraits.
Photo 16968 has no cattle at all — it shows men on horseback with a wrecked cart in cleared bush; 133012 is borderline (one small grazing cow in a wide landscape) but still fits.

Photos 1-3 are clearly cathedral/large Gothic church scenes (interior, facade, spired church in townscape), but 324228 is a postcard of the Invercargill public gardens with only a small domed building in the distant background — its subject is a garden, not a cathedral.

First three show unmistakable pearl necklaces; 2113358's large translucent graduated beads may be glass rather than pearls, but the fit is ambiguous on a clearly related necklace portrait so it counts as true.

Photo 1517510 does not fit: it is a coastal seascape with small distant steamers/fishing boats, no battleship or warship visible; the first three all show clear warship subjects (destroyers at wharf, H.M.S. New Zealand, cruiser at anchor).

211467 (Fijian thatched huts) and 520268 (villagers carrying a woven fale roof) fit; 376271 shows Kent oast houses with tiled conical kiln roofs (only an incidental thatched hay rick), and 105454 shows a NZ coastal settlement of weatherboard/iron baches in scrub with no thatch at all.

403658 is borderline: it is a mixed contact sheet (house exteriors, gardens, portraits) rather than a single room, but several frames are genuine room interiors, so it counts as a partial fit; the others are unambiguous interiors (a sunporch twice, a bedroom).

All four fit: a car-parts warehouse, a petrol/motor-oil supplies forecourt, a service station with batteries and fuel, and a garage workshop; the last (117522) shows repair servicing rather than supplies but is a clearly related automotive scene.
All four are clear sand scenes — dunes, drift hills, an advancing sand face, and rippled sand flats — so the tag fits every photo, including the edge picks.

All four fit: 242537 and 1259199 show thatched bures/fale prominently, 211314's town panorama contains many small but visible thatched dome fale (confirmed by zoom), and 113108 is mainly a river landscape yet has a clear thatched fale at its right edge.

All four photos prominently show WWI-era New Zealand soldiers in service uniform (lemon-squeezer hats, tunics, puttees); the two that include civilian women still feature uniformed soldiers as central subjects, so the tag holds throughout.

Photos 1-2 feature prominent fireplaces, photo 3 is a stair-hall interior with a brick fireplace visible through the doorway at right (borderline but a genuine fireplace is in frame), while photo 130058 is an outdoor road/bridge landscape with power poles and hills — no fireplace anywhere.

Photo 1837388 does not fit: it shows an arched hallway with a cabinet opening onto a tiled room with plain ladder-back chairs (a hall/kitchen passage), not a living room; 520283 is a borderline veranda-lounge tea scene but reads as a living space.

Photo 117779 does not fit: it shows a menswear shop interior with racks of ordinary suits and a customer being fitted, not costumes; the other three are genuine ceremonial/theatrical/fancy-dress costumes.

All four fit: a Dutch town canal with windmill, a canal lock/sluice works, Venice's Grand Canal at the Rialto, and a straight embanked ornamental water channel in Invercargill gardens (the weakest but still canal-like fit).

550864 and 35510 are unmistakable penguin colonies, but 243991 shows nesting king shags/cormorants (long necks, white wing patches, stick nest) with no penguins visible, and 259573 shows a herd of quadrupeds (goats) on a barren cliff face above the sea.
1047161 does not fit — it is a hillside panorama of Wellington harbour and city where chimneys are at most tiny incidental details, not an identifiable subject.

All four photos feature prominent towers (Delft gate towers, a crenellated gatehouse tower, Canterbury Cathedral's towers, and a church bell tower); even the borderline picks are tower-dominated compositions.

All four plausibly fit: 430598 is a classic canyon vista and 348878 a steep-walled chasm, while 129694 (eroded badlands pinnacles in a gully) and 15953 (an open river gorge with bluffs) are borderline but clearly canyon-related rather than different subjects.
Photo 742206 shows a taxidermy display of shags/cormorants, not ducks; 129304 is borderline (ducks small in a park-pond scene) but genuinely contains many ducks.
All four are staged taxidermy habitat/display groups (bird dioramas); the two stereographs show visible table edges and backdrop but are still clearly diorama displays.
All four photos genuinely show trucks; even the borderline ones (129682's edge-cropped truck on a rural road, 130741's quarry scene) contain clearly visible trucks, with 1809003 a textbook example.
All four photos show a tractor as a clear visible subject; 358478 is primarily a service-station scene but a tractor dominates the foreground, so it still fits.

All four clearly show steam locomotives — 349332 is a tight boiler-top detail but unmistakably a locomotive under steam, and the others show locomotives at a station, in a cutting, and hauling trains through a valley.

First two clearly show wooden shipping crates (rail wagon loading; cased cargo on a ship's deck), but 292285 is a filing cabinet with cardboard document boxes and 224087 is a botanical specimen photo of flower spikes in a shallow planting tray — neither is a crates subject.

All four show structures visibly under construction (cranes, framing, formwork, scaffolding, site materials); 1023244 is the most finished-looking (Parliament House near completion) but rooftop crane and shear-legs make the construction state clear.

All four fit: two nests with eggs, a ground colony blanketed in thousands of seabird eggs (55478, verified by zoom), and 1794554 is borderline-but-true — mostly hatched chicks in the nest, with one unhatched speckled egg clearly visible.

All four are military parade scenes a visitor would accept: 1013908 and 112586 show columns actively marching, while 186617 (troops standing in ranks at a field review) and 1791979 (wharf ceremony, officers pacing past troops at attention) are static-formation edge cases but clearly related.

The first three are clear portraits of people wearing coats (fur-trimmed coat, houndstooth overcoat, belted overcoat), but 122371 is a wide interior view of a garment factory with workers at cutting tables — no identifiable coat is the subject, so "Coats" does not fit.

Photos 166505, 172351 and 423883 clearly show uniformed brass bands (tubas, cornets, trombones, drums) performing or posed; 118043 is the General Motors NZ band, but it is a string band — banjos, guitars and mandolin, no brass instruments visible — so "Brass bands" does not fit.

No clear misses: 433674 (Pisa Baptistery) and 227457 (domed gallery ceiling) are unambiguous, while 1794581 and 17781 are borderline-but-acceptable — distant exhibition towers and mansion turrets whose ogee cupola roofs read as small domes rather than a principal dome.

Photo 223965 does not fit at all — it is a botanical specimen photo of leaves and orchid-like flowers on a white background, with no people or facial hair; the other three are portrait composites of moustached/bearded men.

773153 shows a flock of gulls (white bodies, black wingtips) on a lawn, not pigeons, and 402812 is a formal garden lily pond with a fountain and a duck-like bird at its edge — no pigeons; 25752 is clearly kereru (NZ pigeons) at a nest, and 391046 is the classic Trafalgar Square pigeon flock in flight.

Photos 1-3 fit: a billowing geothermal plume, a distant eruption-style smoke/ash column over a lake, and dense smoke from a bush burn-off; photo 168533 clearly does not fit — it shows a waterfall with rising water spray/mist, not smoke.
All four clearly show crowds at sports grounds or watching outdoor events; 1045969 is the weakest since no play is visible, but the crowd massed on a school lawn reads as a sports-day audience.
First three are clear garden scenes (flower-border path, Milton Domain gardens, staked vegetable garden); 53786 is a close-up botanical plant study against a dark cloth backdrop, not a garden scene.
All four photos clearly show a concrete dam under active construction (formwork, cranes, cableways, workers' camp); no mismatches even at the weak edge of the set.

Photo 1747305 is captioned "The War Memorial, Durie Hill, Wanganui" — a memorial/observation tower that merely resembles a water tower; the other three (Hawera tower, Invercargill tower and waterworks, and a lattice tank stand under construction) fit the tag.

195459 is unambiguous (literal iron "Coronation Gates"); no photo clearly misfits, but 1034726, 531657 and 531654 are ceremonial arches/gateways (night ceremonial gateway, Government House foliage arch, castellated street arch) with no actual gate leaves — borderline gateway-sense fits rather than literal gates.
All four clearly fit: Château de Chillon, a moated crenellated stone manor, the ruins of Cowdray House, and a distant but unmistakable view of Windsor Castle across the Thames.

All four are commercial delivery/goods vehicles (butcher's truck, panel van, Evening Post newspaper service car, freight truck), though 116959 is borderline — a passenger-seated service car whose newspaper signage is what ties it to delivery.
All four fit; 520205 and 1717663 strictly show fur stoles/wraps over cloth coats rather than full fur coats, but both are clearly related fur-outerwear portraits.
All four show flags flying; 131461 is the weakest fit — primarily a decorated city street where the flags/bunting are small background elements rather than the subject.
First three are unmistakable tiered wedding cakes, but 362478 shows a display of ornamental vases with floral arrangements — no cake in view.

360730 genuinely shows large wall-hung maps of New Zealand at an exhibition; 175797 is a photomicrograph of a rock thin-section (Hauynophyre, Monte Vulture) and 133368 is a close-up of geological strata in a rock face — neither contains any map.

351305 is a genuine storm shot from a ship's deck with huge breaking waves, but 1517467 and 1517468 show small steamers on calm-to-lightly-rippled grey seas — ships at sea, yes, but no heavy seas visible in either.

Photos 1-3 clearly show clergy (Bishop Selwyn and Bishop Patteson in clerical collars, and a bishop in rochet and cap at a church door), but 1794624 is a studio portrait of a young man in an ordinary suit and necktie with no clerical dress or church context.
All three are genuine woolshed shearing scenes; 432332 is very dark/underexposed but shearers bent over sheep and loose fleece are still visible, and 1799149's caption confirms shearing.

All four fit: 270305 and 214772 are posed school class portraits, 1046010 shows massed uniformed pupils assembled in a schoolyard, and 18809 (Central School Invercargill) is mainly a building view but includes a clear group of school children lined up in front, a borderline-but-acceptable fit.

Photos 1, 2, and 4 are unmistakable posed rugby team portraits (striped jerseys, trophy/ball); photo 3 (116402) is borderline — a large lawn-bowls club gathering rather than a tight team lineup, but as a posed sports-club group on the green with bowls it still reads as correctly tagged.

All four fit: a veiled nurse portrait with medal, a faded Victorian woman in pinafore-and-cap nursing-style uniform (borderline nurse vs domestic servant but clearly related), an album photo captioned "Nurse and Nancy" of a uniformed nurse holding a baby, and two WWI-era nursing sisters in capes and white veils.

All four fit: 54126 shows hay being elevated onto a stack, 16448 shows a stooked field with wagons being loaded (arguably grain harvest but clearly related), 1841420 shows a woman bagging hay beside a haystack, and 1389595 (captioned "Greek women working in fields") shows women gathering cut fodder with a field stack — borderline but still a related haymaking/harvest scene.

All four are genuine industrial interiors (paper mill, seat-assembly floor, motor-body workshop); 72458 is the borderline case — a rough timber bush-sawmill shed rather than a conventional factory, but still a clearly related machinery-filled mill interior.
All four fit; 321337 and 327307 show the Kelburn cable tramway (a funicular rather than a street tram, but the tramcar is the visible subject), while 726995 and 1287485 show street trams plainly.

1701804 is not on a ship's deck — it shows people standing on a seaside wall, captioned "Watching the Procession on the Marine Parade"; the other three are genuine shipboard deck scenes (posed passengers by a lifebuoy, a contact sheet of deck-games frames, and whalers cutting blubber on deck).

125675 is a textbook shop interior; 360724 is likely an exhibition-hall trade display of tinned goods rather than a working shop, and 118015 is a close-up grocery display counter in a rough timber space — both borderline but clearly shop-like merchandise-display scenes, so accepted.

All four clearly show band rotundas; 1187628 is the weakest — a wide view of The Square, Palmerston North where the rotunda is a smaller background element beside a fountain, but it is still plainly visible and the tag fits.

All four fit "Rock formations": limestone outcrops among trees (2371537), a rocky bluff face with flax (54690), a close-up of laminated rock strata with a scale rule (121697), and a sculpted wave-worn rock shelf on a beach below cliffs (132848) — the last two are study/scene shots rather than showpiece landforms but rock is clearly the subject.
432159 does not fit — it is a sheep-dipping/drafting yard scene full of sheep with no pigs visible; 2184870 shows slaughtered pigs laid out for a feast, which still reads as pigs.

None of the four fits "Railway stations": 225762 shows a port/customs street (NZ Steam Navigation Co, ship chandlers), 20695 a Palmerston North commercial main street, 122357 a Texas Oil Company depot, and 22140 the Feilding town square gardens — no station building or platform is visible in any.

All four fit; 132021 and 132502 are borderline — their rocky outcrops may be headlands or tidal islets rather than distinct islands, but both are clearly island-like coastal scenes rather than different subjects.

2198539 does not fit — it is a crowd of civilians posing on a hillside above the harbour at old Port Chalmers with no identifiable gun even under magnification; the other three clearly show artillery (memorial display cannons, a field-gun crew in the desert, and truck-mounted WWI anti-aircraft guns).
All four are clear international-exhibition court interiors (three from the 1876 Philadelphia Centennial NZ section, one similar NZ court), so the term fits every photo.

369283 is a studio portrait of a girl holding a dark plush teddy bear (dangling jointed limbs, toy not live animal) — a child-with-toy portrait, not a dog; the other three genuinely show people posed with dogs.

All four fit: 20156 and 282203 are unmistakable cave mouths, 169357 is a cave interior looking up a shaft, and 122649 is borderline but passes — bathers in a lagoon photographed from inside a cave mouth, with another cave opening visible in the background cliff.

398787 clearly does not fit — it is inscribed "Lt. Genl. F.M. Colville, C.B." and shows an army general with a "43" regimental forage cap; 458900 is a naval/merchant-navy officer in a peaked cap, a related maritime fit counted as true.

380322 clearly does not fit: it shows a sleeved fur jacket/coat (belongs under the separate Fur coats tag), not a stole or muff; 454750 is a white fur cape/wrap, borderline but stole-adjacent enough to pass.

143531 is a textbook side-view profile and 370763 a deep semi-profile that loosely fits, but 1482722 is a mostly-frontal three-quarter headshot with both eyes to camera and 2085307 is an over-the-shoulder pose with the face turned back toward the viewer — neither shows a profile.

451843 clearly does not fit — a small boy in a belted tunic with a large lace collar and giant bow (Fauntleroy style), no sailor elements; 370746 is an older teen in an actual naval uniform and 1495948 a sailor-capped, sailor-collared child in a pinafore (possibly a girl), both close enough to pass.

125338 does not fit — it shows a woman posed beside two artworks hung on a weatherboard wall (paintings on display, not a studio backdrop); 208736 is borderline, a plain mottled painted canvas rather than a scenic backdrop, but still counts.
Photo 107628 has no haystacks at all — it is an open tussock/scrub landscape with bare hills and a lone stump; the other three are clear stook/harvest/haystack scenes.

All four are portraits with long hair worn loose; 713366 is the most borderline since the sitter's long hair hanging down her front partly blends with her cloak's dark thrums, but it still reads as long loose hair.

359678 (farmer with two horses hauling a wooden sledge) and 176029 (draught-horse team ploughing) contain no tractor at all — both are horse-drawn farm work; 117208 is a weaker fit where tractors appear small amid power-line construction across farmland.

432660 clearly does not fit — it shows a rustic pole-and-thatch garden gazebo with no glass structure in frame; the other three all show a glasshouse prominently (vinery interior, winter-gardens conservatory at frame edge, and a portrait posed in front of a timber glasshouse).

First three are unmistakable heavy-horse teams in working harness; 110827 is borderline — a three-abreast coach/wagon team on a bush road with lighter-built horses than true draught stock, but still a clearly related horse-team-in-harness scene.

All four fit: three unmistakably show children holding or pushing toys (toy horse on wheels, stuffed animal plus doll, stuffed dog); 242385 is the weakest — a motion-blurred child standing on a chair clutching a small dark hand-held object that reads as a toy but cannot be positively identified.

27857 shows ducks swimming on a bush stream (no seals) and 107719 shows two boys on a low-tide reef where the seal-like shapes are smooth featureless boulders, while 16157 and 16259 are genuine hauled-out sea lions in tussock (Burton Bros, Auckland Islands) that fit the tag.

All four show railway yards or station yards with sidings and rolling stock; 24119 is a Dunedin city panorama but the yard dominates the left of frame, and 18133 (Studholme Junction) is a small country junction rather than a marshalling yard yet still clearly a yard scene with wagons on sidings.

Photo 354970 does not fit — it shows the Anderson corner general store with utility poles and no visible petrol pumps; the other three clearly show bowsers or service-station forecourts (349267 is a rustic roadside bowser refuelling scene with a Shell truck, still a fair fit).

First two are plausible heavy-engineering workshop interiors, but 116895 shows pump/turbine machinery being installed in a power-station-style concrete hall and 116791 is clearly a motor-car assembly plant (car engines, manifolds, chassis), not railway workshops.

123255 (staff group posed with locomotive) and 191432 (crew posed with engine) fit, but 19385 shows a locomotive and bridge with only distant civilian onlookers, and 19319 is a station scene of boys posed by the tracks — neither shows railway staff as the subject.

All four show truss/trestle bridges over water (19984 is even captioned "Paremata Railway Bridge"); 195453 (captioned just "Bridge, Fairlie") and 290800 lack visible tracks so rail vs road use is unconfirmed, but both are clearly related bridge scenes rather than different subjects.

195900 clearly does not fit — it shows bullock teams hauling logs past a bush building with track only incidental in the corner; 18833 (sawmill bush tramway) and 540862 (mass-concrete works with construction tip-wagons) are borderline but read as related construction scenes.

First two clearly show tracks entering tunnel portals, but 1068378 is a blurry steam locomotive in a bush gorge and 712363 is a line curving through a gorge under a footbridge/flume — no tunnel visible in either.
All four clearly show dams: a large hydro dam with reservoir, a curved concrete dam under construction, a completed dam crest walkway, and a small weir-style dam spilling across a bush stream.

1514762 clearly is not cargo handling — it shows crew flensing a whale (cutting blubber with long knives) on a whaling factory ship; 1517444 and 1517412 pass only loosely as deck scenes dominated by rigged cargo derricks, while 1453657 (wool bales on wharf wagons beside a ship) fits squarely.

All four fit; 942795 is borderline — a natural rock arch in Buller Gorge captioned "The Cave" rather than an engineered tunnel, but the road passes through the opening so it still reads as a tunnel scene.

227449 is not a library — it is a skylit art-gallery/exhibition room hung with framed pictures over display cases, no books; 117338 looks more like a bookshop than a library but passes as an ambiguous book-lined interior.

224461 and 125436 are unmistakable kitchens (plate racks, crockery, dishwashing); 224837 is the borderline one — a tiled scullery/washhouse with deep tubs and a copper boiler, no stove or food prep visible, but still a kitchen-adjacent domestic sink room rather than a different subject.
105495 does not fit: it shows a flat grassy tussock plain between bush-clad hills with no visible sand or dune forms; the other three clearly show sand dunes or dune country.

28231 clearly does not fit (a coastal view of sea, headlands and eroded cliffs, no crater) and 346530 shows a bush-covered valley ringed by hills with no visible volcanic features; 1058285 is steaming geothermal flats rather than a crater but is a closely related volcanic scene, and 31903 is an unmistakable steaming crater interior.

22233 (Fern Arch, Buller Gorge) and 2029160 (The Looking-Glass, Akaroa, with a clear window through the headland) are true arches, and 128284 is an ambiguous-but-related cleft sea stack whose converging masses read as an arch; 20253 does not fit — it is the Franz Josef Glacier terminal ice cave, an arched cavern of ice, not rock.

27037 does not fit: it is a close-up of ferns, flax and daisies with no hill landscape visible; 127325 is borderline (scrub-and-flax hillside rather than forested hills) but clearly related, so it passes.

389395 clearly does not fit — it shows a temporary photo display pinned to boards in a plain community hall with casually dressed viewers, not a museum; 779184 and 778611 are Victorian exhibition-hall courts with glazed display cases, museum-like enough to pass as borderline.
129068 (inscribed "Ohaki Spring") shows a hot-spring sinter terrace with clear reflective water pools rather than mud pools; the other three are genuine bubbling-mud/mud-cone scenes.

All four are mounted-specimen museum displays; 23685 is the weakest fit — a dried elephant fish specimen on a labelled plinth, a specimen mount rather than classic taxidermy, but still a preserved-animal display.
